extracted.intended_audience: geologists, legal historians, reform-minded legislators, and educated general readers interested in marriage law and rock weathering
extracted.subtask_description: Field-study-style research using dated tombstones to estimate rates and modes of rock weathering in urban churchyards, with methodological discussion of legal/historical context in an adjacent article on married women's legal position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of marriage forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Polygyny; rudimentary monogamy; pure monogamy — described as successive types in marriage development, with legal and social consequences for family order and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains each type's characteristic limits and legal arrangements (e.g., polygyny allows fatherly indulgence inside household while enforcing mother's chastity; rudimentary monogamy involves graded wifehood with different legal protections as in Roman law; pure monogamy recognizes only one man-one woman legally). Useful as a typology for analyzing legal treatment of marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common-law merger of married woman's legal being
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the old common law 'the married woman's whole legal being [was] merged in that of her husband' — husband became legal owner of her property, had control over her actions, body, earnings, and children, while being responsible for her crimes and debts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a baseline standard/criterion for critique and reform: identifies the scope of legal disabilities to be removed or limited by statute and jurisprudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-by-state statutory variation in married women's rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed enumeration of differences among States (e.g., in 28 States a married woman has separate ownership of property owned before or descending to her; in 21 States earnings are separate property; counts for will-making rights, ability to sue/be sued, insurance, homestead acts, business control, trusteeships, debt liability, guardianship, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these concrete statutory indicators as measurable dimensions to compare legal status across jurisdictions; the page gives specific numeric tallies to illustrate heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical advice: ascertain statute and actual judicial practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The first thing for every married woman to do is to find out the statutes of her own State respecting her position, and then learn the actual practical bearing of the laws in any point that touches her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because statutes may be interpreted restrictively by lawyers and judges, legal rights on the books may differ materially from practice; the criterion for relying on a right is evidence of its enforcement and common legal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of corresponding responsibilities with increased legal independence
rubrics_metrics.description: As women attain personal rights (separate property, earnings, business control), they are expected to assume corresponding personal responsibilities (liability for antenuptial and postnuptial debts, partial or equal liability for family support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats legal equality as a bundle of correlated rights and duties; legislative reform should consider both gains and liabilities to avoid incomplete or inconsistent results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for uniformity of marriage and divorce law across States
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be some uniformity of law, as to marriage contract and its dissolution by divorce, in the different States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues as a normative standard for reform: avoid situations where parties assume obligations under one state's law and evade them under another; uniform rules would reduce legal inequities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and secondary principles for legal adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Two principles to guide adjustment of marital law: (1) the primary need of family unity as a condition of social order, and (2) the secondary need of increasing measure of personal independence for women within that unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these two guiding principles as evaluative criteria when judging or drafting statutes — balance family unity against women's personal independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reliable compilations to document inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Compilation by reliable lawyers of present laws with an indication of all inequalities and injustices (example: work by Almy and Fuller for Massachusetts) is a great help toward reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation/standard for advocacy and legislative change: produce authoritative, documented comparisons to reveal injustices and support reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tombstones as proxy data for rock-weathering rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Data of provisional value may be obtained from examination of tombstones freely exposed to the air in graveyards in cases where their dates remained still legible or might be otherwise ascertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological recommendation: use dated monuments to estimate long-term weathering; recognize limitations (urban influence, monument orientation, past restoration). Provides an accessible, field-available dataset for measuring surface loss over decades/centuries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for urban vs country differences in weathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Disintegration in towns may be an exaggeration of the normal rate due to mineral acids (sulphuric acid) from chimneys; but town dust and grime may form crusts that protect surfaces from acid attack; temperature extremes may also differ due to smoke-retarded radiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using town tombstones, evaluate both aggravating (acid rain) and mitigating (protective crust, altered temperature extremes) urban factors; do not assume simple scaling from urban observations to natural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term experiments can be skewed by exceptional events
rubrics_metrics.description: An exceptionally powerful cause (for example, a severe hailstorm) might make the loss during a short interval considerably greater than the true average of a longer period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution in interpreting short-duration exposure experiments; prefer longer observation periods or account statistically for episodic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials classification for monumental stones
rubrics_metrics.description: The materials employed for monumental purposes in the district are of three kinds: 1. Calcareous (marbles and limestones); 2. Sandstones and flagstones; 3. Granites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use material classification as primary axis for comparative weathering analysis because each class exhibits distinct modes and rates of decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marble weathering phases
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of weathering in white saccharoid marble presents three phases sometimes observed on the same slab, viz., superficial solution, internal disintegration, and curvature with fracture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these phases as diagnostic stages when assessing marble condition; identify which phase dominates to infer causes (chemical solution vs loss of cohesion vs mechanical failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of exposure and orientation on weathering rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate at which transformation (loss of polish and surface granularization) takes place seems to depend primarily on the extent to which the marble is exposed to rain; slabs facing northeast and with projecting architraves to keep off rainfall retain inscriptions legible for a century or longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing monuments, control for orientation and shielding; sheltered orientation is a major predictor of inscription legibility and slower surface solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective crust dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: A peculiar gray or begrimed crust often forms on marble; while unbroken the crust may keep inscriptions legible, but beneath it cohesion of grains is destroyed and once the crust breaks decay becomes rapid; crust may crack polygonally and blister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret crust presence ambivalently: it retards superficial solution but hides internal disintegration — conservation decisions should consider the risk of sudden exposure and accelerated decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microstructural susceptibility of saccharoid marble
rubrics_metrics.description: Common white saccharoid marble consists of rounded granules of clear transparent calcite with well-developed rhombohedral cleavage and apparently no amorphous matrix; grains are not extraordinarily cohesive and a small fragment placed in dilute acid was entirely dissolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microstructure (granularity, lack of matrix) indicates high susceptibility to both chemical solution and internal disintegration; select stone types accordingly in durability assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variability among marbles (Carrara-like vs saccharoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: A snowy white, more translucent marble (possibly Carrara or strongly saccharoid variants) dissolves without crust and escapes the internal disintegration that accompanies crust formation in common saccharoid marble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different marble varieties show distinct weathering responses; do not generalize from one variety to all marbles — material provenance and texture matter for predicted durability.
